To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the brain activity in the latency range of the P1-N2 components of the ERP could be modeled by a single moving equivalent current dipole or by two stationary dipole sources in a spatio temporal dipole model.

spatial attention enhances the amplitude of the P1-N2 complex, and that this enhancement can be explained by a model with two stationary dippers, one in the mesial posterior and the other in the lateral posterior brain regions.
spatial attention enhances the amplitudes in the P1 and the N1 latency range, and that the late negative ERP component is topographically distinguishable, and not a late P3.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the spatio-temporal aspects of brain activity related to spatial selective attention and memory search, and the results are discussed in the context of current models of the functional organization of the brain.
the spatio-temporal aspects of the brain activity associated with the processing of visual information in the human brain.
the topographical aspects and the neural source of ERP components reflecting selective spatial attention and working memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the P1-N2 complex reflects a general attentional enhancement of the brain's response to visual stimuli and that the late negativity reflects the search of memory.
the brain activity associated with spatial attention and memory load is topographically similar but not identical.
the P1-N2 complex and the N2-P3 complex represent two different processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the topographic analysis of ERPs to visual stimuli is useful in distinguishing between different cognitive functions, such as spatial attention and memory.

the topographical aspects and source analysis of ERPs to spatial attention and memory tasks are consistent with the idea that these processes are mediated by overlapping but not identical brain mechanisms.
attentional and memory processes are reflected by overlapping but topographically separable brain activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topographical aspects are important for the analysis of brain electrical activity, as they allow for the disentanglement of overlapping components.

the brain activity in the latency range of the P1-N2 components is topographically similar to the P3 component, and the P1-N3 components can be explained with the same dipole models that are used to describe the P3.
the P1-N2 ERP components are not the result of a single, fixed, and localized neural source, but rather reflect activity of a distributed neural network.
